seam_notes: The loop has no input door. The only mid-run levers are pause and resume, and direction is fixed at construction. An UNDESIGNED injection path exists and works: pause is honoured after the current iteration, and resume with a statePath rehydrates from run-meta.json + harness-config.json on disk rather than from the lost in-memory orchestrator (a deliberate crash-safety choice), so an operator can pause, hand-edit the config the resume reads, and resume with a changed direction while the run keeps its identity and history. It has no record of the intervention, no ordering guarantee against the pause it races, and leaves nothing in the run's history showing that a person intervened or when. Deliberately not proposed here: building the injection door. That is a direction-sized change to the harness's control surface, not a coverage fix, and it is the owner's call.
measure: None taken, and that is the finding. The claim 'a first-class boundary injection beats hand-editing a config file under a race' is a design argument about operator outcomes, and nothing in this tree counts operator outcomes.
falsifier: The instrument that would settle it half exists: the harness emits lifecycle events including harness:paused, and every run writes durable run-meta.json. Counting, per run, whether a pause was followed by a resume of the SAME run or by a fresh start — and how many areas were replanned when it was a fresh start — yields the number this technique moves: work discarded per operator intervention. Until that counter exists the verdict cannot be better or not-better. RETURN CONDITION: when the harness gains that counter, or when an operator reports discarding a plan to change direction.

This tree's module comment states the sharper rule - 'the sampling is part of the instrument': a judge scoring TIMING on a strip whose spacing the sampler made uneven is grading the sampler.
measurable: regularity of the strip as a function of the cap, for a fixed capture length. Arm A (technique as written): a bigger cap is a better sample. Arm B (this tree's rule): spacing decides.

Structural fact: an even-as-possible pick is uniform only when (available-1) % (kept-1) == 0, so when available-1 is prime the only uniform picks are 2 and all. structural_fact: the tree's default cap of 10 against a 14-frame capture is not a sloppy number - it is the only kind available, because 13 is prime and admits no middle uniform pick. Declaring the irregularity is therefore the correct engineering response rather than a fallback, and this tree does it three ways the technique had no rule for: kept-of-available not a bare count, gaps published when spacing is not uniform, and available/uniform reported as NULL rather than guessed when the caller supplied the frame paths.

subject: cross-provider-benchmark-operations
seam: src/lib/visual-gen/input-gate.ts (DEFAULT_GATE) via src/lib/vision/providers/ollama.ts
truth: 60 images labelled by eye (6 pass / 54 fail), 10 ambiguous excluded; 2 repeats each, temp 0, num_ctx 8192
target: bad inputs let through at the refusal line (score >= failBelow)
result: All three arms 100% GPU-resident at 8k with nothing co-resident, so residency was not a confound at this window, and the technique changed nothing here (not-better). What the arena returned: as shipped (refuse < 5), the incumbent lets 16/54 bad inputs through, gemma 20/54, MiMo 8/54, all with 0/6 good refused. The incumbent ranks best (AUROC 0.998 vs gemma 0.991, MiMo 0.966): at refuse < 8 it lets 3/54 through and at refuse < 9 1/54, still 0/6 good refused. MiMo cannot go below 3/54 without refusing good inputs (refuse < 9: 3/54 through, 1/6 refused), because it scores flat UI emblems 9 while naming their dark backdrop as a defect. MiMo is 3.8x faster (p50 0.92s vs 3.55s) and 8 GB smaller, but the gate guards a minutes-long paid job, so speed does not buy anything here. All arms: 60/60 identical across repeats, 0 unparseable.
finding: DEFAULT_GATE {passAt 7, failBelow 5} was fitted on the DashScope chain (qwen.ts 2026-08-22), but router.ts PLAN puts ollama first for recognize, and .env pins qwen3.8:27b. A threshold is fitted to its grader.
next: Proposed, not shipped: a per-grader refusal line (qwen3.8:27b: failBelow 8). Held because the positive class is 6 images and a false refusal blocks generation; grow the pass set to >= 20 before moving the line.

subject: image-to-3d-input-gating
technique: a threshold is fitted to its grader (cross-provider-benchmark-operations)
seam: src/lib/visual-gen/input-gate.ts DEFAULT_GATE -> GRADER_THRESHOLDS
target: bad inputs admitted by the local grader at the refusal line
result: Truth set grown to 88 (19 good / 69 bad) with 28 original fixtures (tracked). qwen3.8:27b at failBelow 5: 21/69 bad admitted, 0/19 good refused; at failBelow 8: 7/69 admitted, 0/19 refused (floor held). 88/88 identical across repeats. Round 1 (6 good) had suggested 9; the grown set refuted it (a good robot scored 8), which is why the line is 8.
finding: Cropping is the grader blind spot: chest-up crops on white score 9, no line below 10 catches them. MiMo-9B ties at 8 (6/69) but 8/19 good scores sit on the line: no margin, no row.
next: A crop-specific check (subject bbox touching the frame edge) would close the blind spot mechanically; not built.

subject: table
technique: loading-and-empty-states (a payload that arrived but cannot be decoded is not empty)
seam: src/components/layout-lab/steps/ArchetypeStep.tsx ViewPanel chart branch -> decodeChartPayload
instrument: throwaway vitest arena rendering ViewPanel over every stored chart-step payload in ~/.pof/pof.db (read-only dump, live + revisions), same inputs through HEAD (A) and the change (B), plus 11 synthetic shape controls
target: stored chart payloads that arrived but rendered as 'No data yet'/'No numeric data yet'
floor: stored payloads that rendered a chart (tolerance 0); genuinely unproduced data ({} or bookkeeping keys only) still reads 'run Produce'
result: n=178 real rows over 16 chart steps (27 live, 151 revisions). A: 12/178 present-but-undecodable payloads shown as empty (3 live: status-knockback Balance holds a controlBudget record with none of dps/totalDamage/referenceHit; two bestiary Encounter Balance rows carry derivedBalance and no balance field; 9 revisions of the same classes, one an items Economy revision from before the economy field existed). B: 0/178 empty, 12/178 ShapeMismatch naming expected vs received. Floor held: 166/178 charted in both arms. Controls: absent and {} stay empty; string, number, list, renamed keys, wrapped rows, scatter record, waveform string all empty->mismatch; histogram with none of its keys went chart (a row of zero bars from `?? 0`) -> mismatch.
finding: The seam could have falsified the rule if stored payloads never mis-shaped (the spec linter guarantees stub produce() output decodes). It held: the live mis-shapes all came from model-authored produce, which the linter cannot see. The knockback case also shows the view descriptor, not the payload, can be what is wrong (a control status routed through a DPS chart); saying 'run Produce' there sent the user to a button that cannot fix it.
